name: PFMBench against ProteinGym on ESM-2 and ESM3: ESM-2 half explained, ESM3 input asked upstream
description: Review of discrepancy-4db3e5d24233e19b, revision 3: investigating, reported upstream.

attributes.rationale: ESM-2 is explained by aggregation: with the same plain mean over the same 217 assays, ProteinGym's per-assay file at commit 144fe22 gives ESM-2 650M 0.438 against PFMBench's 0.439 (ESM-C 600M 0.434 against 0.434). ESM3 is not: like for like the gap is 0.414 against 0.483. PFMBench Table 4 labels ESM3's input as sequence only, while ProteinGym conditions ESM3 on the AF2 structure, which would explain the gap, but PFMBench's released code builds ESM3Model without sequence_only and always tokenises the AF2 structure, misaligned with the sequence window on the 16 targets longer than 1,022 residues. Which configuration produced 0.414 was asked upstream.
attributes.awaiting: PFMBench's answer on which ESM3 input produced the Table 4 ProteinGym score.
attributes.source_locator: expansion-p3-pfmbench: Table 4 (ProteinGym zero-shot) and the released code (zeroshot/model_interface.py on_test_epoch_end; ESM3Model construct_batch); ProteinGym DMS_substitutions_Spearman_DMS_level.csv and scoring_ESM3_substitutions.sh at commit 144fe22, as checked on rewire-bio/rewire-benchmark-data#280

review.reviewer_note: Recorded by a Claude agent; the upstream question was posted by the repository owner on 2026-11-18; no human source review claimed.
review.method_note: Recomputed plain means from ProteinGym's per-assay file and read PFMBench's Table 4 and released scoring code (issue 280).
review.note: Records where the discrepancy stands. No result value or status was changed.
